symptom: A video whose codec/container needs normalization leaves the import card at preparing with no real progress, can consume all CPU, and can leave an orphan ffmpeg after the app/window/project exits.
direct_cause: electron/assets/videoImportNormalize.ts starts ffmpeg with a private spawn without AbortSignal, process-group cleanup, progress parsing, priority lowering, or a bounded thread count; localFileImport awaits it before copy progress begins.
class_root: The shared process-owner invariant is missing at the import normalization boundary: every ffmpeg used by a cancellable import must be launched through the bounded process runner and every caller must share one cancellation signal before any output can be published.
affected_population: Native-path video imports from canvas file selection, asset-library upload, Finder drag/drop, and paste on macOS and Windows.
Byte-path video imports and MCP nomi_asset_import that normalize a non-playable codec/container.
Existing projects whose lazy playback-heal path invokes the same normalization function.
entry_points: Canvas file selection and native upload
Finder drag/drop and paste through copy-files
internal_only_reason: The invariant is Nomi's process lifecycle and asset publication contract; official editor documentation informs the UX direction but cannot decide Nomi's IPC, project-binding, or scratch-file ownership.
invariants: No import normalization ffmpeg is spawned directly from an asset module; it runs through runBoundedProcess.
The import request signal, sender destruction, project binding invalidation, and quit drain all abort the same process before publication.
Cancellation removes the partial output and scratch directory and is not treated as a missing or failed asset.
A playable video in an unsupported container is remuxed with stream copy; libx264 is selected only when the video codec is not in the injected machine-playable set.
Conversion progress is emitted through AssetLocalizationEvent.phase=converting with a monotonic duration ratio.
Conversion uses below-normal priority and at most max(1, CPU count - 2) threads.

door_reduction.why_not: The two localFileImport doors remain because native-path and byte-path imports have different input ownership and publication boundaries. The eight other direct spawns are unrelated export, frame, audio, speech, trim, and fixture paths; they remain a frozen baseline for 0.25 and are not import-transcode callers.

generality_proof: All checked import surfaces converge on importLocalFile or the shared videoImportNormalize functions. The changed normalization boundary owns codec/container selection, the only ffmpeg launch, the shared cancellation signal, and progress projection, so provider, caller, platform, and stored-asset variations cannot reintroduce an unbounded import ffmpeg without bypassing the static regression gate.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own spawn, process-group/taskkill cleanup, timeout, abort, progress callback, and optional priority lowering for bounded child processes.
Own the single import normalization decision and choose remux versus libx264 based on the existing playability reason.
Thread the import request signal and conversion progress into every native and byte import before publication.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Native canvas, asset-library, Finder, and paste uploads call the same transcodeFileToPlayableMp4IfNeeded boundary.
Byte imports call ensurePlayableVideoBytes, which delegates to the same bounded normalizer.
MCP nomi_asset_import resolves a safe real path then calls importLocalFile with the request signal.
Lazy playback healing invokes the same normalizer and receives the same bounded process behavior.
This is timeline editing/export behavior explicitly outside the import normalization scope and remains a frozen direct-spawn baseline.
Frame extraction is a separate derivation path and is not called by localFileImport.

recurrence.reason: Any non-playable codec or unsupported container can reach the same private spawn through several import surfaces, and a window/project/app lifecycle event can occur during every long transcode.

prevention.invariant: Import normalization launches no direct ffmpeg process; it supplies signal, progress, low-priority, and bounded output options to runBoundedProcess.
prevention.failure_mode: Abort rejects as cancellation, terminates the process tree, and removes the incomplete output/scratch directory before the caller can publish an asset.
prevention.strategy: Keep process ownership at the existing shared runner and thread one request signal from IPC/MCP lifecycle to normalization, so no caller can silently outlive its window, project session, or application.

legacy_paths.rationale: The private unbounded spawn is deleted in the same implementation commit; no fallback launcher remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The bundled ffmpeg/ffprobe version is retained; the defect is application-level process ownership and lifecycle, not a dependency capability gap.

migration: No stored-data migration is required. Existing assets continue to read; new imports use remux or libx264 according to the existing playability reason. Existing direct-spawn non-import paths remain a documented 0.25 baseline.
residual_risks: Windows real Electron and the 4K HEVC walkthrough remain unverified until the separate quiet-walk fix is merged into origin/main.
The eight non-import ffmpeg spawns remain outside this change and must be migrated or retired in 0.25 before the baseline can be removed.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The shared process runner is the earliest boundary that can enforce abort, process-tree cleanup, bounded output, optional progress, and low priority for every import normalizer caller.
